study type: Pilot project / Prospective observational study using registry data
exposure: Receiving perinatal care at American Association of Birth Centers (AABC) Strong Start sites
outcome: Client perceptions of care (knowledge, values, experiences)
Trust in pregnancy, birth, and parenting
Achievement of preference for vaginal birth
Breastfeeding at discharge through 6 weeks postpartum
Client-reported respectful and accessible care (e.g., time for questions, feeling listened to, involved in decision making)
cohort: 553 Medicaid beneficiaries who received prenatal care at 34 American Association of Birth Centers (AABC) Strong Start sites between 2015 and 2016.
finding: Medicaid beneficiaries receiving prenatal care at AABC Strong Start sites demonstrated high levels of desired engagement and reported receiving respectful, accessible care and high-quality outcomes.
mod_finding: Beneficiaries achieved their preference for vaginal birth (89.9%) and there were no variations in cesarean birth by race.
